lines.en: I walk sideways; it is steadier that way.

lines.zh: 壳太重，我走一步停一下。
lines.en: The shell is heavy; I step and pause.
Thin claw trails mark the sand behind me.
I drag my shell through the seagrass.
A wave comes, so I grip the sand.
Eight legs make a messy sort of walk.

lines.zh: 我背着一间会走路的房子。
lines.en: I carry a walking house on my back.
Wet sand is easier than dry sand.

lines.zh: 我顺着湿沙一路摸过去。
lines.en: I feel my way along the wet sand.
Shell mouth down, so water stays out.
I cross the red meadow to the beach.
One claw raised like a little flag.
I shove a small pebble out of the way.
I know the way back by my own tracks.

lines.zh: 壳卡在石缝里，我倒着退。
lines.en: My shell jams; I back out of it.
I follow the tide line up the shore.
Feet push wet sand; I shuffle on.
The sun heats my shell a little.

lines.zh: 整只蟹都藏好，只余眼柄。
lines.en: Everything hides but my two eye stalks.
The shell is damp inside; perfect.
I lift a claw and groom my feelers.
I am used to this shell's spiral.
I hear the wave pulling back.

lines.zh: 沙粒钻进壳口，我抖一抖。
lines.en: Sand got in, so I shake it out.

lines.zh: 我在等一只更漂亮的壳。
lines.en: I am waiting for a prettier shell.
Seagrass shadows sway; I ignore them.

lines.zh: 我用背磨光滑壳的内侧。
lines.en: My back polishes the shell from inside.
The sun warms my shell right through.

lines.zh: 我数着退潮留下的水洼。
lines.en: I count the pools the tide left behind.
My eye stalks swivel once.

lines.zh: 有只小虫爬过我的壳顶。
lines.en: A tiny bug crawls over my shell top.
Even dozing, I grip the sand.
Stay back; my shell is not thick enough.

lines.zh: 你影子盖住我了，我害怕。
lines.en: Your shadow covers me and I am afraid.
I back away two steps, still watching.

lines.zh: 你弯下腰，我就缩进去了。
lines.en: You bend down and I pull inside.

lines.zh: 你手里有壳吗？没有就走。
lines.en: Got a shell? No? Then off you go.
I raise my claw only to block.

lines.zh: 你踩的地方是我的沙滩。
lines.en: Where you stand is my beach.
I do not bite anyone; I only hide.
Your footsteps are far too close.
I will come out once I am sure it is safe.
A hairline crack now splits my shell.
The blow makes me clamp myself shut.
One of my legs is gone.
Blood seeps into the sand at my shell.
In pain I grip my own claw.

lines.zh: 壳要是碎了，我就没处躲。
lines.en: If the shell breaks, I have nowhere to hide.
I limp sideways, slower now.
That kick is written on my shell.
I shrink to the very back and stay.
The knock on my shell was far too loud.
Is that empty shell meant for me?
Your hands smell faintly of fish.
I reach out one claw to test.
That scrap of meat fell on the sand.
A shell tempts me more than food does.
I step closer, then half a step back.
Leave it and go, and then I will eat.

lines.zh: 这壳的大小看起来合适。
lines.en: That shell looks about my size.
I am hungry, but I fear you more.
Do not reach out; I will retreat.

lines.zh: 你的脚尖碰到我的壳沿。
lines.en: Your boot tip struck the rim of my shell.
My shell tipped, so I set it right again.
I sidestep; I will not argue with you.

lines.zh: 你这么大，撞一下我就翻了。
lines.en: You are huge; one bump flips me over.
I am gripping the sand; do not push.
Shell against shell rings out crisply.
I pull in and wait for you to leave.

lines.zh: 你的靴子压到我的腿了。
lines.en: Your boot pressed down on my leg.
I retreat to the water's edge and stop.

lines.zh: 别踩，壳裂了我就没家了。
lines.en: Do not step; a cracked shell is no home.
I tap my shell and listen for an answer.
Her shell is one size bigger than mine.
Two shells touch and sidle along together.

lines.zh: 你愿意换壳给我看看吗？
lines.en: Would you trade shells with me?
I touch her claw gently with mine.
Two hermit crabs, and one empty shell.
When the tide drops, our eggs wash seaward.

lines.zh: 她缩进去了，是答应了吗？
lines.en: She pulled in — is that a yes?
We must find bigger shells first.
I stay beside her shell and wait.
My big claw pinches this thing.
Too heavy for my claw to lift.
The shell is too small; I tried twice.
I drag it over beside the crevice.
Food goes into the shell mouth first.
Can I actually fit into this shell?
Before swapping, I must test the size.
I have it; do not try to take it.
I measure the width with my feelers.
Drag it home and enjoy it slowly.
An empty shell glints over there.
Meat lies on the sand, unclaimed.
I creep toward that shell.
The target is small; my claw can hold it.
There is food there, and also risk.

lines.zh: 我先看看周围有没有人。
lines.en: I check around for anyone first.
That shell shines more than my old one.
I slowly extend a claw to reach it.
It sways in the water; I wait for it to settle.
Worth the risk; I am hungry.
I fix on that shell's opening.
One step closer, and then I pinch.

lines.zh: 我算着潮水什么时候退。
lines.en: I work out when the tide will retreat.
It drifted away, so I must follow.
Small as it is, it is worth a lot to me.
Shell low, every leg drawn tight, I wait.
My claw is already open wide.
A shadow falls over me and I freeze.
One more moment would be safer.
I approach as quietly as I possibly can.
I pinch you once, only once.

lines.zh: 大螯是为了吓人，不是杀人。
lines.en: The big claw threatens; it does not kill.
Reach inside, and then I pinch.
After pinching I retreat into my shell.

lines.zh: 这只螯比看上去更有劲。
lines.en: This claw crushes more than it seems.
Do not squeeze my shell; I hit back.
This pinch only makes you pull your hand back.
I raise my claw; you step back first.
It stings, does it not? I did warn you.
I cannot beat you, but I can pinch.

lines.zh: 我从沙里爬出来，壳先出。
lines.en: I climb out of the sand, shell first.
This is the edge of the red meadow.
One or two of us, never more.
First I look for a shell worth living in.
The tide just went out; the sand is wet.
Three points of life, very light indeed.
I look at the world from inside my shell.
Seagrass nearby; I like that.
I head for the water step by step.
Born already carrying my own home.
The shell grows hot to the touch.
The shell lands and I hear it crack.
Water fills the inside of my shell.
The blast flips me shell over legs.
An arrowhead wedged into my shell's spiral.
Light on my shell makes me go numb.
No scrap of food for a long while.
Lightning hit the beach and my shell rang.
No sand, no sea, only falling.
